content.title: Robby Ferrufino Park Playground Renovation
content.summary: The City of Arvada is hosting a Playground Concepts Open House on June 25, 2026, at Robby Ferrufino Park to present designs for a new all-abilities playground. The project aims to create an inclusive and accessible play environment that encourages independent play and social interaction for children of all ages and abilities, building on community feedback gathered during previous outreach efforts. Robby Ferrufino Park honors the memory of a compassionate young boy and continues to serve as a community space for connection and play.
content.body:
## Robby Ferrufino Park Playground Concepts Open House

Join the City of Arvada and the project design team for a Playground Concepts Open House for the future all-abilities playground at Robby Ferrufino Park. During the open house, attendees will have the opportunity to review conceptual playground designs that were developed based on community input gathered during the Playground Design Workshop on April 7 along with other project outreach efforts.

**Where**: Robby Ferrufino Park playground pavilion, located at [8925 W 74th Ave.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hkrBkUcByfmYYSM88)

**When**: Thursday, June 25, 2026

**Time**: Stop by anytime between 5:30 and 6:30 p.m.

This is an open house-style event, so there will be no formal presentation. Community members are welcome to stop by anytime between 5:30 and 6:30 p.m. to view the concepts, ask questions, speak with the project team, and share feedback. Input received during the open house will help inform the continued development of the playground design.

![Robby Ferrufino Park playground renovation open house flyer with date, time and location details.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=7736)

## Project background

Robby Ferrufino Park ([7435 Carr Dr.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/U7Zge5EyHMXM4KWPA)) is getting a new all-abilities playground designed to be welcoming, inclusive, and accessible for people of all ages and abilities.

Located at the west end of the park, the existing playground needs to be replaced. Rather than a traditional playground renovation, this project will create an all-abilities play environment that goes beyond minimum accessibility standards to support meaningful, independent play for everyone.

The renovated playground will serve as a neighborhood destination where children and caregivers of all abilities can play together, explore, and connect in a shared space.

![Playground structure with blue slide and red supports at Robby Ferrufino Park.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=7181)

1. [The story behind Robby Ferrufino Park](#tab6811d922-5df6-4fa2-b103-4f562ec9b826_0)

Robby Ferrufino Park is named in memory of Robby Ferrufino, a young boy whose generosity and spirit left a lasting impression on his family and community.

Robby was diagnosed with cancer as a child and spent time receiving treatment at Children’s Hospital in Denver. Even while facing serious illness, Robby became known for his kindness. He often gave away gifts he received to other children in the hospital who were also undergoing treatment.

Robby also found moments of joy through the Sunshine Kids, a group that helps children with cancer experience special activities and outings, including trips to Denver Broncos games.

Robby passed away in 1989 at the age of 10. In his memory, his family created a memorial fund and continued efforts to support children facing serious illness.

Today, Robby Ferrufino Park stands as a tribute to his compassion and the positive impact one child can have on others.

As the City plans a new all-abilities playground at Robby Ferrufino Park, the project continues the park’s legacy as a place where children of all backgrounds and abilities can play, connect, and build community.

### What is an all-abilities playground?

An all-abilities playground is intentionally designed so people with physical, sensory, cognitive, social-emotional and communication disabilities can play alongside their peers, not apart from them.

The goal of the new playground is to create a play environment that:

- Encourages active, independent play
- Supports social interaction and connection
- Offers a variety of play experiences for different ages and abilities
- Allows children and caregivers to participate with dignity and choice

The design will include an interconnected play circuit, accessible surfacing, inclusive play features, and shaded areas to support comfort and usability throughout the day. By creating a space where everyone can play together, the playground will promote empathy, understanding and a sense of belonging within the community.

## Community engagement

Community input is a key part of designing the new all-abilities playground at Robby Ferrufino Park.

An initial Speak Up Arvada survey conducted in 2022 helped inform the project’s early direction. Building on that feedback, the City will focus engagement efforts on in-person opportunities that allow park users and stakeholder groups to actively participate in the design process.

Community engagement opportunities:

- **Playground Concepts Open House on June 25 at Robby Ferrufino Park**
  - The on-site open house will provide the opportunity to review conceptual playground design that were developed based on community input gathered during the Playground Design Workshop on April 7 along with other outreach efforts.
- **Playground Design Workshop on April 7 at Warder Elementary School**
  - More than 100 community members joined us for an interactive workshop that gave children and families the chance to explore playground ideas and share what kids of play equipment they'd like to see at the new all-abilities playground.

Community engagement is planned for winter through summer 2026 and will include in-person workshops where children and families can share ideas, explore play concepts, and provide feedback on playground features. We really want to make sure we are listening to the voices of the children who will use the playground to ensure the design supports meaningful, independent play for a wide range of abilities.

The City will also work to connect with nearby neighbors, local schools and community organizations that serve individuals with disabilities to help ensure a broad range of perspectives is considered.

Information about upcoming engagement opportunities will be shared on this webpage as the project moves forward.

## Project scope and design elements

The Robby Ferrufino Park playground renovation will include:

- Replacement of the existing playground with a new all-abilities play system
- Inclusive play equipment designed for physical, sensory, cognitive, social-emotional, and communication disabilities
- A complete play circuit that encourages movement, exploration, appropriate risk-taking, and social interaction
- Safety surfacing for improved accessibility
- Permanent shade elements within the play area, where appropriate
- Revised grading to address drainage issues
- Reorientation and restriping of the basketball area, including the addition of a second hoop to create a full court
- Conversion of nearby parking spaces to ADA-accessible parking, along with updated striping, signage, and access routes
- Landscaping with a native plant palette in alignment with the City’s low water use policy
- Select vegetation removal and tree pruning to improve sight lines and enhance safety
- Updates to irrigation infrastructure around the playground

The playground will remain a neighborhood-scaled amenity, slightly larger than the existing playground, and will not include redevelopment of the park’s ball fields or other major park features.

## Project timeline

- Winter–Spring 2026: Community engagement
- Spring–Fall 2026: Design development, construction drawings, and plan review
- Winter 2026: Construction bid advertisement
- Spring 2027: Construction begins
- Summer 2027: Project anticipated to be complete
